title: One Man Spent 20 Years on This Garden — and Nearly Went Broke
description:
Shanghai's Yu Garden (豫园) was begun in 1559 by Pan Yunduan, a Ming official who wanted a private garden for his aging father. It took nearly two decades to finish, and the cost drained the family's fortune — by the time it was done they were close to ruin.

What's left today is about 2 hectares of classic Ming garden-making: rockeries, ponds, dragon-topped walls and pavilions, all now wrapped inside one of Shanghai's busiest tourist bazaars. That's the debate — is a 450-year-old garden worth fighting the crowds for, or would you rather save it for a quieter classical garden in nearby Suzhou?

🧭 Expert Tip: go right at opening or in the last hour before close to beat the bazaar crush, and pair it with the Old Town lanes next door.

上海豫园始建于1559年，潘允端为父亲所建，耗时近二十年、几乎耗尽家财。约2公顷的明代园林，如今被繁忙的商业街包围。你会为这座450多年的园子挤人潮，还是去苏州看更清静的园林？
